_doc: 第1期 (docs/handoffs/structural_simplification_handoff.md §4): one MEANING ×
every SPELLING of it.  The differential-verification corpus in
tests/test_user_cas_invariants.py covers `sessions/*.json` — i.e. expressions
that ALREADY WENT THROUGH.  This file is the other half: the spellings a
researcher can type that have never been measured.
kind:
equivalent — every variant must reach the CAS as the same value.
distinct   — the variants are DELIBERATELY different objects; pinned so a
later 'unification' cannot quietly merge them.
status:
pinned — holds today; a regression breaks the test.
gap    — measured broken on 2026-08-10.  The test asserts it is STILL
broken, so fixing one is a visible, deliberate change (the
`test_known_gaps_are_still_gaps` idiom already used in
tests/test_user_cas_invariants.py).  `gap_reason` records what
the researcher actually gets today.
route:
handler (default) — ask the converter directly.
pipeline          — drive run_interpret_pipeline, for a family whose rule
lives in the request pipeline rather than the
converter (Unicode Greek in a math token). Probing
such a family the fast way reports a fixed defect as
still broken — the §2.2 mistake, in reverse.
An `equivalent` family may agree by all being REFUSED. That is deliberate:
a spelling refused with a reason is better than one silently mistranslated,
and two spellings of one meaning must not differ even in how they fail.

families.meaning: complex conjugate of psi(x)
families.note: CLAUDE.md 'The complex conjugate is one mark with six spellings'. Fixed 2026-08-09; pinned here so the sixth spelling cannot drift out again.

families.meaning: conjugate of psi_n(x), star written before or after the subscript
families.note: The matrix-element spelling: the star sits in FRONT of the argument list.

families.meaning: the (i,j) component of A — two indices
families.note: AUDIT-SUBSCRIPT-SPLIT: a space and a comma are made one spelling at the converter's entrance (_subscript_separator).

families.meaning: the (i,j) component of A, applied at x
families.note: Maxima's subscripted-function form A[i,j](x).

families.meaning: the metric tensor component g_{mu nu}
families.note: A backslash is a boundary of its own, so adjacent commands are never one name.

families.meaning: A_{ij} names ONE index called ij — not the (i,j) component
families.note: CLAUDE.md 'Cost, accepted deliberately'. Pinned so a later 'fix' cannot silently restore the auto-split that turned E_{rot} into E(r,o,t).

families.meaning: q-dot as an independent atom vs the time derivative
families.note: Analytical mechanics: q and q-dot are independent atoms (docs/19). Deliberately NOT the same object.

families.meaning: a·b and a×b are different products
families.note: \cdot lowers to Maxima's non-commutative '.', \times to '~' (cross). Pinned so neither degrades to ordinary multiplication.

families.meaning: a is less than or equal to b
families.note: normalize_relational_ops. The shape \ne/\neq split on (fixed 2026-08-09) — its siblings are pinned here.

families.meaning: a is greater than or equal to b
x squared
square root of x
sine of x
natural logarithm of x
a times b, written with TeX spacing between them
families.note: Spacing is typography, never a factor.

families.meaning: m omega squared
families.note: _separate_adjacent_commands (2026-08-05): without it m\omega^2 merged into the single symbol 'momega'.

families.meaning: phi as a symbol, written with either glyph command
families.note: Both map to `phi`. PHI-GLYPH-SPLIT (open_items) is about DISPLAY, not this direction.

families.meaning: sum of i^2 for i = 1..3
families.note: The 2026-08-10 head-loss bug (`\sum_{i` split at the subscript's own `=`). \limits added 2026-08-10 (it raised a raw pydantic ValidationError before).

families.meaning: e to the x
families.note: Lowers to DIFFERENT code (`%e^x` vs `exp(x)`) that is the same VALUE — so this family is what exercises the ratsimp differential rather than the string short-circuit. Keep at least one such family here.

families.meaning: a divided by b
families.note: Both lower to `a * b^-1` today, so the texts agree on their own; kept because the fraction bar and the slash are genuinely two spellings of one meaning and a divergence here would be a real defect.

families.meaning: (a+b)*c with sized delimiters
families.note: Fixed 2026-08-10 (notebook/runtime/latex_typography.py): sizing hints are dropped at the converter's entrance. Was: \big / \Big / \bigl reach the CAS as the SYMBOL `big`: `\big(a+b\big)*c` expands to `big(b*big+a)*c` and the operation reports SUCCESS. \left/\right are handled; their sized siblings are not.

families.meaning: a over b
families.note: Fixed 2026-08-10: \dfrac/\tfrac are normalised to \frac by normalize_command_aliases, which runs BEFORE the BP-9 derivative restorer as well as inside the converter. Was: \dfrac{a}{b} becomes the single symbol `dfracab`; simplify returns it unchanged as a SUCCESS.

families.meaning: a is not equal to b
families.note:
Fixed 2026-08-10: the three spellings are folded into `#` (normalize_relational_ops) and REFUSED with a reason by the parser. The agreement checked here is agreement about being refused — which is a real property: two spellings of one meaning must not differ even in failing. Full support is an ASSUMPTION path (`assume(notequal(a,b))` is what Maxima accepts; `assume(a#b)` fails), not an expression one — recorded in open_items rather than half-built. COMPLETED 2026-08-11: the assumption path now works — `a 
eq b と仮定する` / `assume a 
eq b` register `notequal(a,b)` in the CAS, via the `assumption_canonical` backend hook. So the three spellings agree twice over: refused identically as expressions, accepted identically as assumptions. Was: At top level (not inside a sum subscript) `a 
eq b` lowers to the PRODUCT `a * neq * b`, and `a != b` to `factorial(a)=b`. \leq/\geq are handled (see relation_le); 
e is not.

families.meaning: sum of i^2 for i = 1..3, bounds written in either order
families.note: Fixed 2026-08-10 (LatexConverter._script_order): the two orders are made one spelling at the converter's entrance, for every limit-taking operator. Was: The superscript-first spelling loses the BOUNDS: `sum(i^2, i)`, and simplify then fails in Maxima. Reversed script order is ordinary LaTeX.

families.meaning: sum of i for i = 1..N, bounds written in either order
families.note: The bare (unbraced) script is the spelling _script_order has to read without braces to lean on.

families.meaning: integral of x dx from 0 to 1
families.note: Fixed 2026-08-10 (LatexConverter._script_order) — this was the worst of the eight: the only one that returned a plausible WRONG NUMBER rather than a broken symbol. Was: The superscript-first spelling silently loses the bounds and evaluates as an INDEFINITE integral: simplify returns `x^2/2` (a SUCCESS) where the answer is 1/2.

families.meaning: the symbol a, wrapped in a font command
families.note: Fixed 2026-08-10: font wrappers are unwrapped with balanced braces, EXCEPT when the whole spelling is in the backend's constant table (\mathrm{i} stays the imaginary unit). Was: The wrapper merges with its content into one symbol (`mathita`). Measured in REAL saved sessions: Maxima's own display writes the imaginary unit as \mathit{i} and the BCS scenario's g' as \mathrm{g'}.

families.meaning: partial derivative of f with respect to x
families.note: Fixed 2026-08-10 (maxima_derivative_latex.partial_subscript_to_frac): the subscripted operator is rewritten IN PLACE into the operator fraction, leaving the operand exactly as written. Was: `\partial_x f` lowers to the PRODUCT `partial(x) * f` — a derivative silently becomes a multiplication.

families.meaning: d/dx of an operand that carries arguments or brackets
families.note: The bracket-losing trap: the first attempt at partial_subscript_to_frac moved the operand into the numerator and had to re-emit it, so \partial_x (f+g) became \frac{\partial f+g}{\partial x}. Pinned so a future rewrite cannot reintroduce it.  MEASURED INSUFFICIENT 2026-08-13: re-applying the exact slip (rewrite into the numerator, re-emit the operand without its brackets) does NOT fail this family — its operand is CALLED, and the numerator form reads a called operand correctly since the 2026-08-11 _trailing_operand fix. Only a BRACKETED operand shows it, which is what partial_applied_to_bracketed_operand below now carries. The family written in answer to a slip did not cover that slip.

families.meaning: d/dx of a bracketed sum of two functions
families.note: STRUCTURAL-SIMPLIFICATION 残作業 2 (2026-08-13): the bracket-losing slip of 2026-08-10 was found by probe, never by a test, and the family added afterwards used a called operand instead of a bracketed one — so a faithful re-application of the slip still passed. Measured: with the numerator rewrite restored, `\partial_x (f+g)` becomes `\frac{\partial f+g}{\partial x}` = ∂f/∂x + g, and THIS family is what fails. A rewrite must be exercised with an operand whose brackets carry meaning; a bare or called name cannot show a lost bracket.

families.meaning: d/dt of an operand that carries its arguments
families.note: Fixed 2026-08-11: the numerator's operand is now read by _trailing_operand, the SAME scanner the operator form uses, instead of a name pattern that could not describe an argument list. Was: PRE-EXISTING, found 2026-08-10 and RE-MEASURED 2026-08-11 (the first record understated it: this is NOT only \partial — the ordinary `d` form is broken the same way). The numerator form is read only when its operand is a BARE NAME. The moment the function carries its arguments — i.e. how a wave function or a trajectory is normally written — the `d`s cancel and `simplify` returns a SUCCESS: \frac{d y(t)}{d t} → `y(t)/t`, \frac{\partial \psi(x,t)}{\partial t} → `psi(x,t)/t`. That is precisely the failure BP-9 exists to prevent, still present for every operand that is not a bare name. Already in saved research data: sessions/S-c_redrive_20260731.json holds \frac{dc(k,u)}{dt}, a Heisenberg equation of motion. The operator spelling on the left is correct.

families.meaning: a fraction that merely looks like a derivative
families.note: The guard that must survive every widening of the derivative reader: an unseparated `d` may only be split off a SINGLE-LETTER base, so \frac{delta}{dx} stays an ordinary division (with a warning) rather than becoming 'diff(elta,x,1). Pinned as `distinct` because the two ARE different objects — this is the no-auto-split rule, and widening the operand scanner is exactly when it could be lost.

families.meaning: the mixed second derivative of f
families.note: Fixed 2026-08-11 (_fraction_operand): an operator fraction's operand may itself be a fraction. The chain lowers to nested 'diff, which Maxima normalises to the mixed partial — checked here by CAS DIFFERENCE, not by string, since the two spellings deliberately produce different code. The `d` spelling was the worse half and was recorded as merely loud: \frac{d}{dx}\frac{d}{dy} f actually lowered to `'diff(frac,x,1) * ddy * f` — a derivative of a SYMBOL CALLED "frac", reported as success. Was: PRE-EXISTING (measured 2026-08-10 on the operator spelling, which predates the \partial_x work): a CHAIN of operator fractions is refused with a raw `ValueError: IndexedSymbol index must resolve to a Symbol` — loud, so not silent-wrong, but a raw internal error is the anti-pattern CLAUDE.md names. The single-fraction spelling on the left is correct and is the workaround.

families.meaning: d/dx of a/b, with another term beside it
families.note: The bracket that the chained-operand work could have swallowed: an operator fraction consumes exactly ONE following fraction, so `+ c` stays outside the derivative. Pinned as distinct because these two ARE different expressions.

families.meaning: omega times t
families.note: Fixed 2026-08-10 (ui/interpret_common.normalize_request_greek): math tokens are normalised too. `latex` gets the TeX spelling; a `canonical` carrying Unicode is dropped and re-derived from it, rather than growing a second Unicode→canonical map in that layer. Was: `normalize_request_greek` (ui/interpret_common.py) already converts Unicode Greek ONCE per request, before any interceptor — but only for tokens of type `text`. A MATH token's latex is left alone, so `ω` typed into the formula box (or handed over by the handwriting OCR) reaches Maxima as the symbol `ω`, which no declared `\omega` will ever match. The same shape as the 2026-08-02 fix that created that function (INTEGRAL-VAR-NOTATION), one token type over: a ROUTE split, not a converter defect.

families.meaning: a fraction as Maxima's own tex1 writes it
families.note: Fixed 2026-08-10: TeX's infix \over is read by scanning the enclosing group in both directions. This closes the display round trip for every fraction Maxima's tex1 emits. Was: Maxima's tex1 emits `{{a}\over{b}}`; re-inputting the system's OWN DISPLAY leaves `\over` as a symbol. 24 occurrences in sessions/*.json — the display round trip (R3) does not close for fractions.

families.meaning: the 2x2 matrix [[2,1],[1,2]], in every spelling a researcher writes
families.note: TEX-MATRIX-INPUT (2026-09-10). 9 spellings reached the CAS and only the ';' literal worked, so the round trip did not close: the system PRINTS \begin{pmatrix} and could not read it back. The others were not refused but silently mangled (\\ dropped, two rows fused; \pmatrix eaten by \pm). See notebook/runtime/matrix_environment.py.

families.meaning: brackets vs vertical bars: a matrix, a determinant
families.note: The delimiters say WHICH QUANTITY it is. Vertical bars are the determinant — a SCALAR (this one is 3) — so reading every environment alike would register a scalar as a 2x2 table. Pinned distinct so a later 'they are all matrices' simplification cannot merge them.
